Definition: akin to σκαίρω (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus):--leap (for joy).
BiblicalUsage: Skirtazo means to leap, and it is the leap of a child and the leap of the persecuted. The babe leaped in Elizabeth's womb when Mary greeted her, and leaped again for joy, and Jesus tells His disciples to leap for joy when men hate them, for their reward is great in heaven.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the leap of the unborn John is the first joy of the gospel, because the child knew his Lord before he could see Him.
